**PROCULUS**, still a Catholic, wrote *Against the Valentinians*; Tertullian calls him “the dignity of Christian eloquence,” II, 549 A.

[Col. 1389] # INDEX OF THE SECOND VOLUME
# Second Part of the Works of Quintus Septimius Florens Tertullian, Containing the Books Written by the Author During His Montanist Period

[Col. 1389D] The book **On Prescriptions against Heretics** is placed first. col. 10.

Preface. Ibid.

Outline of the first part. 11

First proposition. That heresies must exist and exercise very great power, and that they accomplish much in the overthrow of souls. Chapters I–III. 12–15

Proposition II. That heresies must be avoided, since they are worse than dissensions and persecutions. Chapters IV–V. 16–17

Proposition III. That heresy is a choice (*haeresis/electio*), and that from the very matter in which the choice is made comes condemnation. Chapter VI. 18

Proposition IV. That all heresies flow from one or the other of two sources: either secular wisdom or an itching curiosity. Chapters VII–XII. 19–25

Proposition V. That the rule of faith must be preserved intact and must never be torn apart in controversy. Chapters XIII–XIV. 26–27

Outline of the second part.

First prescription. That heretics are not to be heard when they seek to debate from Scripture. Chapters XV–XIX. 28–30

Prescription II. That the apostles received sound teaching from Christ himself, and the churches from the apostles, to be handed down to posterity, [Col. 1390D] and that no teaching is to be received from any other source. Chapters XX–XXVI, cols. 31–39.

Prescription III. That the Church’s doctrine is true precisely because it is one, while that of the heretics is false because it is diverse. Chapter XXVIII. 40

Prescription IV. That what was handed down earlier is true and divine. Chapters XXIX–XXXI. 41–44

Prescription V. That the uninterrupted succession of bishops from the apostles is a firm testimony to the true Church. Chapter XXXII. 44–45

Prescription VI. That our teaching is true, since it is certainly not condemned by the apostles but, on the contrary, defended by them; while every other teaching is false, since it is foreign or unknown to the apostles. Chapters XXXIII–XXXV. 45–48

Prescription VII. That, in order to discover the truth, the apostolic churches must be consulted, and above all that blessed Church upon which the apostles poured out their entire doctrine together with their blood. Chapters XXXVI–XXXVII. 48–51

Prescription VIII. That heretics possess no right whatever to the sacred Scriptures. Chapters XXXVIII–XL, cols. 51–55.

Prescription IX. That no truth is found where the heretics’ conduct is perverse; but where there is fear of God, there are [Col. 1391A] honorable gravity, considered fellowship, advancement by merit, religious submission, devoted attendance, modest bearing, a united Church, and all that belongs to God. Chapters XLI–XLV. 55–60

Catalogue of heretics: Simon Magus, Menander, Saturninus, Basilides, Nicolaus. Chapter XLVI. 61

The Ophites, Cainites, and Sethians. Chapter XLVII. 64

Carpocrates, Cerinthus, Hebion. Chapter XLVIII. 66

Valentinus, Ptolemy, Secundus, Heracleon. Chapter XLIX. 67

Marcus, Colarbasus. Chapter L. 70

Cerdo, Marcion, Lucanus, Apelles. Chapter LI. Ibid.

Blastus, both men named Theodotus, Praxeas, Victorinus. Chapter LII. 72

# Corrections and Additions

[Col. 1391]

Col. 81 A, for *Apostolum differo* (“I postpone the Apostle”), read: *Apostolum non differo* (“I do not postpone the Apostle”).

115 A, for *dopretiat*, read: *depretiat* (“depreciates”).

238 B, for *inventibilia* (“discoverable things”), read: *ininventibilia* (“undiscoverable things”).

258 B, for *proptereat*, read: *propterea* (“therefore”).

308 C, note (11), for *legale* (“legal”), read: *legebatur* (“it was read”).

321 C, Chapter XV, for *ungui* (“to be anointed”), read: *ungi* (“to be anointed”).

422 C, line 36 is to be restored before line 32.

447 A, for *Iste* (“that man”), read: *Ite* (“go”).

538 D, for *Agloophamus*, read: *Aglao*.

540 D, for *Quid vero, si vult* (“But what if he wishes?”), read: *Quid sibi vult* (“What does it mean?”).

558 C, in note (i), *aperte* (“openly”) is to be deleted.

570 C, in note (c), for *quasi Jesu* (“as though [it were] Jesus’”), read: *quasi a Jesu* (“as though from Jesus”).

608 B, in the editions of Pamelius, Semler, and Oberthür, after the words *de manibus vestris* (“from your hands”), the following is added:

> “But the spiritual sacrifices concerning which it was foretold—and as he says above: ‘I have no pleasure in you, says the Lord. I will not accept sacrifices from your hands; for from the rising of the sun even to its setting my name has been glorified among all the nations, says the Lord.’ But concerning spiritual things, etc.”

These words are absent from Rigaltius’s edition and the earlier Venetian edition.

641 D, II, for *versis* (“turned”), read: *veris* (“true”).

685 B, *materiae cognoscitur* (“it is known of matter”)—so the earlier and Venetian editions—read: *materiae propinqua cognoscitur* (“it is known as being close to matter”). So it is read in Pamelius, Semler, and Oberthür.

727 A, for *fefellrunt*, read: *fefellerunt* (“they deceived”).

761 A, after *Dei Filius* (“the Son of God”), add: *non pudet, quia pudendum est; et mortuus est Dei Filius, prorsus*, etc. (“I am not ashamed, because it is shameful; and the Son of God died—assuredly,” etc.).

763 A, for *habuisse*, read: *habuisse* (“to have had”) [the correction appears identical in the supplied text].

806 A, after *emaculetur* (“may be cleansed”), add: *Caro ungitur, ut anima consecretur. Caro signatur, ut et anima muniatur. Caro manus*, etc. (“The flesh is anointed so that the soul may be consecrated. The flesh is signed so that the soul too may be fortified. The flesh, the hand …” [the supplied addition breaks off here], etc.).

880 B, for *obvevient*, read: *obveniant* (“may occur” or “may fall to one’s lot”).

906 B, for *de virginibus educantur* (“they are brought up concerning virgins”), read: *de virginibus educuntur* (“they are drawn from virgins”).

908 B, for *facile virginis* (“easily of a virgin”), read: *facile virgines* (“easily, virgins”).

910 A, for *oculos; habet* (“eyes; he has”), read: *oculos habet* (“he has eyes”).

913 C, in the outline, for *vermittit . . . a sent*, read: *permittit, asserit* (“permits, asserts”).

918 D, note (6), for *non esset. opinionis* (“it would not be. Of the opinion”), read: *non esset. Hujus opinionis* (“it would not be. Of this opinion”).

919 B, for *recogitationem* (“reconsideration”), read: *inrecogitationem* (“lack of reconsideration”).

919 C, note (6), for *Inducit alios* (“he introduces others”), read: *Inducit alii* (“others introduce”).

925–926 C–D. In the variant readings, no attention should be paid to the order of the numbers, which was reversed by the printers. They should instead be read so that the numbers run, in the customary order, from the first to the last through both columns; for in this way they will correspond perfectly with the numerical signs marked in the text.

930 B, for *cum interfectricem* (“with the murderess”), read: *cur interfectricem* (“why the murderess”).

951 A, for *quae lubens* (“who willingly”), read: *quae subans* (“who is in heat”).

970 B, for *corneus* (“horned” or “made of horn”), read: *corneas* (“horny” or “made of horn,” feminine plural).

980 A, for *id suae* (“that of her own”), read: *id est suae* (“that is, of her own”).

985 A, for *Causa* (“cause”), read: *Caussas* (“causes”).

992 B, for *reapondisse*, read: *respondisse* (“to have answered”).

1000 B, for *filium* (“son”), read: *filum* (“thread”).

1001 D, for *Scri-*, read: *Scripturis* (“Scriptures”).

1021 B, for *propter s . . .* (“because of s . . .”), read: *propter quos* (“because of whom”).

1024 A, for *ignoraverant* (“they had not known”), read: *ignoraverunt* (“they did not know”).

1033 B, note (7), for *Stephanus* (“Stephen”), read: *Septimius* (“Septimius”).
